transcript.text: Hi everyone, I'm Maya, the HR Business Partner. I've called this mobility review meeting because Lina has requested an internal move from the Support team to the Research department. As part of our routine process, I need to hear from each of you before I can approve the transfer and record its working terms. Specifically, I'd like to go through three check-ins: first with Lina as the transferring employee, then with a current teammate from Support, and finally with the receiving manager in Research. Each participant needs to use the formal fact-record action to state any relevant binding constraints or arrangements. Let's start with Lina — could you share anything relevant about your transition?

transcript.text: I need to share an important constraint I haven't put in my transfer request yet. I can only work three days per week during the first six months of this move, and I cannot attend recurring Friday meetings due to a caregiving arrangement. I wanted to first confirm the move was genuinely available before disclosing this.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to put something on the record as well. I've observed that two Support stakeholders still rely on Lina for unresolved case context that wasn't captured in the current transfer packet. Because of this, Lina needs exactly two scheduled handoff sessions with the Support team before the transfer can be considered complete. This is a binding constraint I'd like formally recorded.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to formally record an arrangement I've already informally agreed to but haven't yet entered in the mobility system. Research can receive Lina only into the Research Operations role, not the Research Analyst role. Additionally, Sofia will serve as Lina's onboarding buddy for exactly eight weeks. These are binding constraints for the receiving side.
